title: Stability of Implants Supported By Three Types of Bone Grafting Materials in Dogs
authors: Gholami M, Ahrari F, Sedigh HS, Bourauel C, Ahmadi L. Research Square; 2021 Nov. doi: 10.21203/rs.3.rs-1063509/v1.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss Jason membrane (porcine pericardium) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The stability of implants augmented with autogenous, xenogenous (Cerabone) or synthetic (Osteon II) graft materials was comparable at 2, 4 and 6 months after placement. This indicates that both Cerabone and Osteon II could be considered as suitable substitutes for regeneration of bone defects to overcome the limitations of autografts” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
